why: What the live MCP door serves, against what dist declares. Each row is a LEAD in the shape lean/leads.json uses — filed, never settled here, because a lead leaves the record only by a verdict. Written by src/scripts/audit-door-surface.ts on every run, EMPTY INCLUDED: an absent file and an empty set are different facts. held.lead: The live door surface is not the one dist declares: 234 contract(s) served against 250 declared, 16 declared and not served (compute_engine, compute_novelty, compute_selftest, decrypt_aead, deposit_wave, fetch_education_jobs, get_build_graph, get_editorial, get_hex_programs, get_publication, get_resources, get_verdict_signatures, run_command, run_security_plan, run_wave, search_trial). A client reading the live list cannot tell a withdrawn door from one that has not shipped, because neither surface says which.
held.owes: a verdict on whether the difference is the expected ship lag or a door lost in a deploy — the counts alone cannot tell those apart, and nothing in the tree measured them before this run

held.lead: One name, two contracts: 5 of 234 compared door(s) answer a different contract handle on the live site than in dist — check_citations (live 9cd13f1d ≠ dist b50a1f2d); compute_address (live b11384cb ≠ dist cd64ef0c); compute_merkle_proof (live 65796ac8 ≠ dist 644a400b); get_conformance (live ae7e547d ≠ dist c2597d21); run_trial (live d3ceee92 ≠ dist 3b6043d2). The handle is this tree's own content address of the contract, so the disagreement is measured rather than diffed, and a client reading one contract and calling the other reaches a different tool.
held.owes: a verdict on whether a shared name may carry two contracts at all; if it may not, the live catalogue owes the reader the version it is serving

A door answers from the baked root (ledgerFacts, sealedAddressOf) or from the one piece its cited key sits in (rowsForKeys) — asking for every row asks for what the ed || 1 door(s) [get_crypto] answer: error: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'key') || 1 door(s) [run_trial] answer: error: uuidna_trial: missing required argument: statement (the tool's own schema declares it required — nothing was computed). A contract that agrees is not a door that replies, and nothing in this tree asked the second question before this run. held.owes: a verdict per GROUP rather than per door: a refusal shared by reads and writes names at most one of their two bars, and whichever half is wrong sends the reader to measure the wrong thing
